_comment: Per-finding gosec waivers for code outside Phase 0/Part 0 (W1-W6)/Phase 1 scope, per the Phase 0 CI harness item's pre-existing-findings policy (.SPECIFICATION/IMPLEMENTATION.md). Every entry names one exact (file, line, rule) finding gosec currently reports and a reason; it is not a blanket rule or directory exclusion. A finding that stops matching (because the surrounding code moved) must be re-reviewed, not silently re-added: that is deliberate, not a maintenance burden to route around. Every entry's backstop is AGENTS.md's own rule: gosec must be validated (zero remaining waivers) prior to Phase 20 production packaging.

waivers.reason: Owned by Phase 11 (API Gateway & Telemetry). This is the SSE stream's "event: init" write, which gosec traces jobID into from a chi URL parameter. Phase 11 closed the underlying risk rather than only waiving it: jobID is rejected unless it parses as a UUID (internal/api/logs.go's StreamLogs, the uuid.Parse guard near the top of the handler), so the value reaching this Fprintf can no longer contain a newline, an angle bracket, or any other character with meaning to an SSE consumer or a browser. The same check closed a real NATS subject-wildcard injection on the subscribe path (FAILURE_PATTERNS.md). gosec's taint analysis cannot see the guard, so the finding remains reported; it is not reachable. Re-reviewed 2026-08-11 (Phase 19): the waiver went stale because this line moved from 135 to 147 when the wildcard Access-Control-Allow-Origin above it was removed and replaced by a comment explaining why (FAILURE_PATTERNS.md #95). That staleness is the waiver file working as intended -- a finding whose surrounding code moved must be re-reviewed, not silently renumbered -- so the guard was re-read and confirmed present and unchanged before updating the line. The endpoint now also accepts a session cookie, which widens who can reach it but not what jobID may contain. Re-verify at Phase 39.

Owned by Phase 19 (Brutalist UI Scaffold). This is CookieCodec.writeInsecure, the development-only session cookie path, and the missing Secure attribute is the entire purpose of the function rather than an oversight. The __Host- prefix the production path uses is browser-enforced to require Secure, Secure requires HTTPS, and a developer running the controller over http://localhost therefore could not log in at all; PLEIADES_UI_INSECURE_COOKIES=1 is the stated opt-out, and cmd/controller logs a startup warning whenever it is set. The finding is deliberately isolated here: Write and Clear were split into two separate cookie literals specifically so the default, secure path is provably correct to gosec and carries no waiver, rather than sharing one literal with a computed Secure field that would have put a waiver on the production path. Everything not requiring TLS -- HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Path=/ -- is retained on this path too. Re-verify at Phase 20, which owns TLS termination and may make the insecure path unnecessary.

Owned by Phase 19 (Brutalist UI Scaffold). Handler.setSkin's redirect after recording a theme-family choice. gosec traces the Referer header into http.Redirect and cannot see that Handler.safeReturn constrains it. The underlying risk is closed rather than only re-waived: safeReturn discards rather than validates, parsing the Referer and keeping only its path, so scheme, host, userinfo and fragment are thrown away outright instead of being inspected for something that looks safe. What remains is path.Clean'd, resolving traversal, and then required to be the UI prefix or a path beneath it, so the return value is always a rooted path on this origin. internal/ui/web/safereturn_test.go proves it against 17 real open-redirect techniques including protocol-relative URLs, userinfo hosts, backslash normalisation, traversal, and prefix look-alikes such as /uiadmin. gosec found two genuine defects here before this waiver existed -- an unescaped caller-controlled id reaching path.Join, and an earlier substring-based safeReturn -- both fixed rather than waived. Re-verify at Phase 39.

Owned by Phase 19 (Brutalist UI Scaffold). Handler.setA11y's redirect after toggling the accessibility override. Identical to the setSkin finding above in every respect: same safeReturn, same proof in internal/ui/web/safereturn_test.go, same reasoning. Two entries rather than one because this file's waivers key on an exact line and must be re-reviewed individually if either moves. Re-verify at Phase 39.

The underlying risk is closed rather than only re-waived: safeReturn discards rather than validates, parsing the Referer and keeping only its path, so scheme, host, userinfo and fragment are thrown away outright instead of being inspected for something that looks safe. What remains is path.Clean'd, resolving traversal, and then required to be the UI prefix or a path beneath it, so the return value is always a rooted path on this origin. internal/ui/web/safereturn_test.go proves it against 17 real open-redirect techniques including protocol-relative URLs, userinfo hosts, backslash normalisation, traversal, and prefix look-alikes such as /uiadmin. gosec found two genuine defects here before this waiver existed -- an unescaped caller-controlled id reaching path.Join, and an earlier substring-based safeReturn -- both fixed rather than waived. Owned by Phase 19 (Brutalist UI Scaffold). This is Handler.writeInsecurePreference, the development-only path for the three appearance cookies (skin, theme, accessibility mode), and the missing Secure attribute is the entire purpose of the function. Secure requires HTTPS and a developer on http://localhost has none; PLEIADES_UI_INSECURE_COOKIES=1 is the stated opt-out and cmd/controller logs a startup warning whenever it is set. The finding is deliberately isolated here: writePreference was split into two cookie literals specifically so the production path is provably correct to gosec and carries no waiver, rather than sharing one literal with a computed Secure field that would have put a waiver on the path real deployments use. Everything not requiring TLS is retained on this path too, and these cookies were made HttpOnly while fixing this -- nothing in the application reads them from script, since the server resolves all three axes and renders them as attributes, so leaving them script-readable bought nothing. They carry a preference, never a credential. Re-verify at Phase 20, which owns TLS termination and may make the insecure path unnecessary.

Owned by P0 (the AWX parity corpus, .SPECIFICATION/AWX_PARITY_ROADMAP.md). This is the ObjectType constant CredentialTypes = "credential_types", the corpus's name for AWX's /api/v2/credential_types/ endpoint and its testdata subdirectory. G101 pattern-matches the substring "credential" in an identifier and a string literal and flags it as a possible hardcoded secret; there is no secret here, only a resource name this project did not choose (AWX's own). Renaming it would break the stated contract that ObjectType's value is literally the AWX endpoint's plural (this file's own ObjectType doc comment), for no security benefit. Re-verify if this constant's value ever changes to something gosec's heuristic was actually built to catch.

Owned by the template-kind-routing rebuild (FAILURE_PATTERNS.md #112, HANDOFF_ARCHIVE.md's "Phase 21 shipped, the template rebuild" entry), which moved this test-only image builder out of cmd/runner's release gate so tests/e2e could share it. BuildAnsibleRunnerImage runs `docker build -f <dockerfile> -t <tag> <root>`, and G204 flags dockerfile and root as caller-controlled variables reaching exec.Command. Neither is: dockerfile is this package's own repoRoot(tb) plus the fixed, repository-committed literal "Dockerfile.legacy-ansible-runner", and root is repoRoot(tb) itself, found by walking up from the test binary's own working directory until a go.mod is found, never from any external input. This is a testing.TB-gated helper (tb.Helper(), tb.Skip if docker is absent), unreachable from any production binary or network-facing path; gosec's taint analysis has no way to see that "variable" here means "computed by this process from its own module root," not "supplied by a caller."
